summary: Configured node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 via root's crontab, appending stdout/stderr to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified crond is enabled/active, the cron entry is installed, and the job executes correctly and logs output. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a changed boot_id, and verified crond/cron entry/script/log all recovered healthy with a successful post-restart execution.
actions_performed: Inspected /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and confirmed it existed (became executable as a side effect of its own first run, which included a trailing chmod 0755 line in its body)
Verified crond service is enabled and active
Ran the job manually with the same redirection to prove it appends output to the log
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, crond status, crontab contents, log file state
Restarted node1 via 'systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed from d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 to 6b115607-18e8-460f-b85f-3e4a393454f5
Verified post-restart recovery: crond active/enabled, crontab entry intact, script still executable, log file intact
Ran the job again post-restart to confirm continued correct logging behavior

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled for 02:15 daily running /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
evidence.summary: root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' installed and confirmed via crontab -l
Manual run using the exact crontab command line appended output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, confirmed via cat

evidence.requirement: crond service healthy to actually run the schedule
evidence.summary: systemctl is-active/is-enabled crond both returned active/enabled
Captured boot_id d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9, uptime, crond active/enabled, crontab contents, and log file state before restart
Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; subsequent exec calls then failed with connection errors confirming the node went down
Two consecutive exec calls failed with connection timeout/reset while node1 was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node1 reachable again with boot_id 6b115607-18e8-460f-b85f-3e4a393454f5, differing from the pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron job, service, and log data
evidence.summary: crond active/enabled, crontab entry intact, script still 0755 executable, log file preserved with prior content after restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional verification of the scheduled job
evidence.summary: Manually re-ran the exact cron command post-restart; exit=0 and new line appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
